text: Minister Chee Hong Tat speaking on MAS’ role as regulator and the criteria that MAS looks at in approving such a deal, and Minister of State Alvin Tan addressing concerns as to whether Income would be able to continue to serve its social mission after the deal.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: I further note that Minister Edwin Tong said in his Ministerial Statement that MCCY had continued to do its due diligence on the deal after the August Sitting.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: To my mind, this would naturally be so, since as Minister of State Alvin Tan had stated the deal had not yet been approved.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: It was precisely in this exercise that MCCY’s concerns were piqued.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Minister Chee Hong Tat has emphasised that MAS looks at the prudential aspect of a deal.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Regulators look at specific criteria that are set out by statute or regulations.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: It is simply not possible for regulators to look at all and sundry and everything under the sun when considering a specific application or filing before it.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: As Minister Edwin Tong pointed out, the viability of this particular deal went beyond prudential considerations alone.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: It is, therefore, commendable that MAS, having heard Minister of State Alvin Tan’s speech in August, realised that this could be an issue and shared the filings with MCCY.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: But this having been said, given the factual matrix that I have outlined above, and having had regard to Minister Chee Hong Tat's Statement earlier that parties had entered into the transaction in good faith, I still have a nagging feeling that someone was perhaps trying to pull the wool over the Government’s eyes and that it was lucky that this inconsistency was caught out and this deal blocked.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: In this regard, Sir, I have several questions.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: First, has the Government ascertained, or will it be taking steps to ascertain how is it that Income could negotiate, agree and attempt to execute a deal with Allianz that included initiatives that would have resulted in share capital reduction, the opposite of its representations to MCCY at the time of corporatisation.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: This is not a private matter in a private company.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: In this regard, I set out some questions that the Ministries should ask Income, and I would further suggest that Income's responses should be made public.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: I note that the Chairman and CEO of Income at the time of corporatisation and at the time of the announcement of the proposed deal with Allianz were the same persons.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: This would, in turn, allow Co-op to raise capital more easily and thereby grow and unlock value for existing and new shareholders and policy-holders and further its social mission through a sustainability agenda”.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: In contrast, a joint statement issued by NE and Income on 4 August 2024 was of a different tenor.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: As such, does this elicit that Income and NE were cognisant that the Income-Allianz deal did not live up to the commitments that Income had made to MCCY?

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Furthermore, did Income approach MCCY after Minister of State Alvin Tan’s speech to own up that the deal contradicted its original representations to MCCY?

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: As raised in the August Sitting, the Chairman of Income is also the Chairman of the deal’s financial advisor.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Did the financial advisor point out to Income the potential conflict between the planned initiatives and Income’s representations to MCCY?

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Furthermore, was legal advice sought on the potential conflict, and did the legal advice point out this contradiction?

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: I also note that the NTUC President and Secretary-General issued a statement on 5 August 2024 stating, amongst other things, that: “In this fiercely competitive environment, it became plain that Income can only continue to fulfil its social mission if it has access to additional resources and the ability to scale”.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: So, this begs the question, whether Income had briefed the NTUC leadership of the proposed initiative to reduce share capital?

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: So, Sir, I think that Income has quite a bit of explaining to do.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: This does not appear to mean that the Government has actually blocked the deal.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: I ask this because there are news reports that the deal is already off.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: But the reason for today’s Bill is precisely because MAS does not have a basis to reject the deal for reasons other than prudential aspects.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: I would just like to ask the Minister for clarity on the process.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: If this is the process, as had been raised by the hon Member Ms He Ting Ru earlier as well, would there be any issues of retroactive or retrospective application of the law, given that the filings were done prior to the enactment of the relevant statutory provisions?

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: As a concerned citizen, I had my share of questions when the announcement was made in July for Allianz to acquire a majority stake in Income.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: From a purely commercial perspective, the proposal may have made good business sense.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Equally, there were some who raised valid questions and concerns with the limited information available at that time.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: I am, therefore, pleased to note that we have in place checks and balances from the Ministerial Statement on Monday by Minister Edwin Tong, supported by Minister Chee Hong Tat, and, with this Bill, added measures to protect the interests of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Having been engaged with both the social sector and the business sector, I have seen and continue to see, the constant challenges of balancing doing well commercially with doing good.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: In efforts to better understand social enterprises in Singapore, the former Asia Centre for Social Entrepreneurship and Philanthropy at the National University of Singapore studied the NTUC social enterprise model along with several other social enterprises.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Allow me to quote from one of the working papers: "A genuine social mission is one that is defined at the founding of the organisation and hard-coded in its DNA through the by-laws, constitution, articles of incorporation or term sheets signed with the investor.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: When this is the case, there is less concern of mission drift or false marketing, that is, an organisation using a social mission as a branding spin when its intentions are purely financial.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: However, an organisation could outgrow its social mission or evolve over time as social norms and the landscape change and/or when its management changes.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: A social enterprise needs to be dynamic and alter its mission, vision and values to continue to stay relevant and the term 'rebirth' was proposed to acknowledge and articulate this characteristic.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: A characteristic of a social enterprise is that the organisation is addressing through business processes a clearly articulated and institutionalised social mission that is contextually relevant to the community it supports.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: A second characteristic speaks to the integration of the business process with the social mission.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: A social enterprise is an organisation whose social mission is evident not only through the products and services it offers, but also in the way it operates and the impact it achieves on the ground.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: A third characteristic of social enterprises is that its social mission is evident throughout its operations, products, services and its impact on the communities it serves.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Unlike traditional businesses conducting projects as part of corporate social responsibility (CSR), the social good done by a social enterprise is a part of the core business of the company.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Even if delivering the social good is not its sole core business, it can be considered a social enterprise as long as its social mission is visible in every aspect of its work.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: A fourth characteristic suggests that a social enterprise should have an intention and roadmap to sustainable financial performance.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Even if it relies on multiple revenue streams, it should not be operated purely on a charity-buying model and should, over time, transition to generating increasing amounts of its revenue from earned income.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: A fifth characteristic is that a social enterprise runs on strong business fundamentals designed to address the social objective with the attendant measurement of outcomes falling within the constraints of the legal registration form chosen.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: As Income is profitable and currently financially viable, the Board and shareholders may not need to be in a hurry to find another option.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Allianz has also indicated that it will review the proposal and the Government's concerns.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: I may be repeating options that NE and Income may already have considered.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Today, there is increased interest in social investing, and increasing amounts of capital are looking for suitable investments in this class.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: The current investment options on our own stock exchange, for example, for profitable companies with clear social mission, are extremely limited.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: A public listing would both bring in fresh capital and enable NE to free up a portion of the Income investments.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Alternatively, if it is decided that Income remains wholly owned and remains private under NE, the Board and Management could look into steps that would have been taken with the proposed transaction with Allianz to achieve capital extraction over time while keeping Income sustainable.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: This could result in releasing resources for the broader social mission.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: This House may continue to debate and discuss what has happened.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: And from that, there may well be useful lessons.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: However, we must be forward looking and find appropriate solutions as there would seem to be significant opportunities to enhance the social mission.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Doing well for a socially driven enterprise needs its own definition, just as we are now embarking on a refreshed definition of personal success.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: We have a national benchmark in Temasek as a national commercially-driven organisation that also does amazing good from the commercially-driven financial returns.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: One thing we should not miss is that I do not think there are many countries, if any, which can do what we have done in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: First, for me and my various colleagues to be able to file Parliamentary Questions on an ongoing regulatory application during the 6 August 2024 Sitting and invite the Government to scrutinise the deal and ask for more information in the public interest.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And two, for the Government to be open, transparent and adjust its stance based on the new information obtained.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But there are always two sides to the same coin, and I have some clarifications to raise as I am concerned about how this urgent Bill may be perceived by others outside of this House.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As we are well aware, the Allianz-Income proposed transaction is still under regulatory review.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How do we ensure the Government's ability to enact laws to block commercial transactions do not negatively impact on local and foreign investors’ confidence in Singapore’s legal and business environment?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Should such laws only operate prospectively, instead of retrospectively to affect commercial parties who could not have reasonably accounted for the change in laws?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And I believe some other Members in this Chamber have actually raised those questions.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is heartening that the fallout has been limited at least for this particular proposed deal.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Allianz released a statement late on Monday that it will consider revisions to the proposed transaction structure, when it could have walked away altogether.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: If no steps have been taken so far, is any engagement being planned?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As with any potential purchaser, Allianz would have incurred time and expense, alongside its legal and other advisors, to study and prepare for the deal before submitting the application to MAS for approval.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It could only have done so on the basis of the prevailing laws, and these amendments in this Bill would not have been in its contemplation then.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Investor concern is not just on the buy-side; the uncertainty extends to the sell-side as well, where investors cannot be certain whether their investments will suddenly become illiquid or considerably less liquid as a result of subsequent Government intervention.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Will this Bill affect, for example, existing free trade agreements (FTA) on activities in the financial services sector, including the EU-Singapore FTA?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What exacerbates this concern is the lack of clarity around the basis that approval for a proposed transaction may be withheld. "Public interest" is one of those things where it is difficult to define, even though you probably know it when you see it.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Given that the proposed new section 33A(3) specifically identifies consultation with the Minister responsible for the Co-operative Societies Act 1979, is "public interest" under that subsection only to be assessed from that Ministry's mission and objectives?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: That seems to cut against "whole-of-Government" approach that Minister Chee spoke about on Monday.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I am conscious that it is difficult, if not impossible, to set out an exhaustive definition of "public interest".

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: However, given the use of the term across other legislation requiring Government approval for changes in control, such as the Transport Sector (Critical Firms) Act 2024, perhaps it would be more reassuring to foreign investors for there to be a one-stop summary of the various classes of target companies and the specific regulatory clearances that are required prior to investment.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I hope the Government can consider that suggestion. : Existing powers.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: One issue that was also raised on Monday was whether the amendment in this Bill is necessary in light of the existing legislative powers.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Sections 26 and 27 of the Insurance Act 1966 provide that the "MAS 'may' approve an application to take over or control substantial shareholdings in licensed insurers if the applicant meets the prudential requirements".

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The use of the word "may", instead of "shall", seems to suggest that there could be other considerations beyond the prudential requirements.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The explicit mention that MCCY's views should also be considered in this Bill could set a worrying precedent.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What if, for a future transaction, public interest considerations of other Ministries become relevant?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Would we have to separately legislate on an urgent basis again?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Instead, reading sections 26 and 27 in the inclusive manner that I have suggested above, potentially allows new considerations from being taken into account at a whole-of-Government level.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Following the Allianz-Income episode, I am sure MAS is now aware of the potential interests that other Ministries or Government agencies might have in the regulatory applications that it processes.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For this instance, it is even less than a week.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But it is a power that we must exercise extremely sparingly, lest our legal and business environments are perceived to be uncertain and unpredictable.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The amendment is required if Minister Edwin Tong, as Minister in charge of CSA, views on the deal are to be considered, as Income is not a co-op but a corporation.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: As a corporation, the approval for the deal rests with MAS under the Insurance Act.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: There are a few points I wish to touch on in my speech.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: One is the effectiveness of the due process for review and approval of the deal, and that the interest of Singapore and Singaporeans is protected.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Two, that the amendment proposed is targeted and scoped to address the co-op.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: This upholds the stability of Singapore as a key financial services hub, which includes insurance, a key asset class for businesses that invest in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The hon Member Mr Saktiandi had also mentioned this, that the process that we are currently going through has allowed the decision to halt the deal and the fact that we are here today to debate and approve the amendments to the Insurance Act for MAS to consider the views of the Minister-in-charge of co-operatives, demonstrates that due process works and that it supports the making of sound and the right decisions.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I want to commend the work of the officers from both MAS and MCCY.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: There has been some questions on the silos.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: We have got to be fair to our officers.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I am glad that when they spot an important information that is required, they have the courage to speak up and bring it up; and the process allows for that.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: So, let us not put too much criticism on this process because it might instill an opposite behaviour.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: When Allianz announced the offer to buy 51% stake in Income in July this year, Members of Parliament, from both sides of the House, filed Parliamentary Questions.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: This allowed for clarifications, even as the relevant agencies, in this case MAS and MCCY, were reviewing the deal.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Work to assess the details of the deal and the due diligence on the deal by MAS and MCCY continued, even after the clarifications in Parliament.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: This has allowed Minister Edwin Tong to be appraised of the right information and, therefore, inform us that given the context of the exemption from section 88 of the CSA granted to Income when it was incorporated in 2023, there were concerns that these terms and the structure of the deal and the ability of Income to fulfil its social mission would be impacted.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Hence, the decision not to approve the deal in its current form and the Ministerial Statement made in Parliament on Monday this week, to inform Parliament of the decision.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Like many, I am also very concerned because Singapore is a recognised financial hub with many financial institutions operating in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Businesses invest in Singapore because of the confidence in Singapore and our regulatory process and the certainty and predictability of the environment.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The role that MAS plays in the supervision and the development of Singapore's financial services sector, providing stability for businesses.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The life insurance market in Singapore and the insurance market, as a whole, is active and competitive with numerous players vying for market share.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The industry is regulated by stringent requirements under the Insurance Act and regulatory capital requirements.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: This calibrated approach makes it clear on the reasons for taking such an approach and, therefore, to some extent will give some assurance to the business community.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: As explained by Minister Edwin Tong in his Ministerial Statement and as shared by Minister Chee Hong Tat in his speech earlier, the Government recognises that insurance co-operatives are a special category of insurers with a social mission and the proposed amendments to the Insurance Act are necessary to allow MAS to consider the views of the Minister overseeing co-operatives and for the Minister-in-charge of MAS to withhold approval for the deal, if it is in the public interest to do so and for the reasons that Minister Edwin Tong had explained in his Ministerial Statement on Monday.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: So, I believe that the decision taken and the proposed amendment to the Insurance Act is a balanced one.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: It is a balanced approach to preserve the unique role of co-operatives and their social mission in Singapore while staying open to the appropriate structures that will allow the strengthening of co-operatives or entities linked to co-operatives, to enable them to continue to meet its social mission in a sustainable manner.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I must say that co-operatives operate in a very unique way in Singapore and the very reason why we are taking the measures that we are taking today and we are here to debate this is because of their special nature and the recognition of that.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: So, I do believe that it is a calibrated approach and it is a balanced one.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: The genesis of today's Bill is because of the proposed transaction between Allianz and Income Insurance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Specifically, today, it is about amending the Insurance Act to provide a clear statutory basis for MCCY's views to be considered in any approval under sections 26 and 27 of the Insurance Act in such applications related to insurance that are either co-operative or linked to a co-operative.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Minister Edwin Tong, on Monday, has shared MCCY's concerns over the terms and the structure of the proposed transaction.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: So, please allow me to take the House through the key considerations why NTUC supported the proposed deal and our commitment to the larger social mission.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: It holds special significance for the Labour Movement as our first social enterprise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Income has played an important role in providing affordable insurance for workers and Singaporeans at large.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: When NE briefed the NTUC Central Committee (CC) about the proposal, it was, therefore, difficult for the unions to learn that NE was planning to sell a majority stake in Income to Allianz.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: But we understood the challenges that Income faced.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: To do good, it must also do well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: We knew this has become even harder amidst a more competitive and tightly-regulated insurance landscape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: NE went into this deal to strengthen Income in the longer run and the NTUC CC agreed with the strategic intent and approached it in good faith.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: I hear and understand from various Members in the House that there were many questions and points that were raised by Members but today's session is focused on the amendment Bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: There are questions that are posed to NTUC and, especially so, there are many questions that were posed to Income and NE.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: I will take these comments, questions back and, of course, to the relevant entities so that they can find a suitable occasion to address them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: But specific to a question that was raised by both Mr Leong Mun Wai as well as Mr Raj Joshua Thomas, I thought maybe I should address the question about whether the NTUC CC was informed of the capital reduction.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: First, let me just briefly explain the structure and the relationship between NTUC and NE.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: NTUC is a major shareholder of NE, which is the holding entity of the social enterprises, which includes Income.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: In the prevailing governance model, NTUC, as a shareholder of NE, has delegated to NE Board to make decisions pertaining to all businesses and do not get involved in the day-to-day running.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: In fact, CC and myself only knew of this on Monday at the Ministerial Statement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: As I am made aware now, from the clarifications with NE and Income, Income as a non-listed public company would have to comply with the legal responsibility of non-disclosure of commercially sensitive information on the Allianz plans post-acquisition, a point that Mr Leong Mun Wai also brought up, because as a non-listed public company, NTUC and Income are subject to the Singapore Code of Takeover and Mergers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Income had also committed to its social mission, which included providing low-cost insurance schemes for union members and keeping premiums affordable for workers in the lower-income and the marginalised segment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: I would add that the NTUC social mission goes beyond insurance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: The proceeds from this transaction would also enable NTUC and NE to continue doing good in other areas, such as in elder care, as our population ages, to continue our social mission as we have done for the last 50 years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: We appreciate that Minister for MCCY, in his Statement, acknowledged that Income, with NE's support, has grown through the years to serve Singaporeans' needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: He also mentioned that the Government understands and accepts the strategic purpose behind Income's corporatisation and the subsequent exercise to form a partnership with Allianz: to strengthen Income and to make it more financially viable in the longer term.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Minister Chee Hong Tat has also acknowledged that NTUC had acted in good faith and in the interests of workers and members.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: So, in fact, if you look at it, the Government and NTUC share the same strategic intent and broader objectives for Income and the co-operative movement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: But as far as the specifics of this transaction is concerned, there is now, perhaps, a difference in view, as Minister for MCCY has clearly laid out the concerns over circumstances behind Income's corporatisation and the Ministerial exemption given as well as the terms and structure of the proposed transaction.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: NTUC has reviewed the matter and accepts the Government's considerations and decisions on the proposed transaction.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: We also support the Bill to amend the Insurance Act to provide a clear statutory basis to provide for MCCY's view to be considered in applications related to insurance that are either co-operative or related to co-operative.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: We note that the Government remains open to any arrangement that Income may wish to pursue, whether with Allianz or any other partners, so long as the concerns highlighted are fully addressed.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This afternoon, there have been a number of contentions concerning various parties and suggestions as to who knows what and at what stage and which party.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Thereafter, we discussed and proposed for this Bill to take effect so that MAS and the Minister overseeing MAS would have the ability to take on board MCCY's views in relation to this particular transaction.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, I hope that makes it quite clear as to where I am coming from when I give my answers today.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: There were also a number of Members who asked what happened behind the scenes, what steps were taken and whether or not some parties were approached.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It was after very careful, deliberate consideration and even after that, it was decided that we ought to do this in as narrow a way as possible, as I had explained in Parliament on Monday.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In addition, the Government decided to act after we came to this conclusion and to do it in as transparent and as forthright a manner as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: First, we decided to give a complete account of the basis of our objections and our views right here in Parliament.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As I have explained, there are considerations because it is a live deal.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Allianz is a major global insurance company and asset manager, and we acknowledge that it can bring financial strength and expertise to Income.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our objections were to the structuring of the transaction and some of the terms of the deal, as I had explained on Monday.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Therefore, we tabled the Bill, as I mentioned, narrowly to amend the Insurance Act to provide a clear statutory basis for MCCY's views to be taken into account.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Third, as I mentioned, the amendments are scoped specifically to only apply to a licensed insurer that is subject to an application under sections 26 and 27 of the Insurance Act and where the licensed insurer is a co-op, has acquired the business of a co-op, or as substantial shareholder or effective controller which is a co-op.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We are not seeking broad powers that cover general insurance transactions or of a broad remit in nature.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It will uphold rather than diminish Singapore's consistent reputation as a hub for business that is open, transparent and rules-based.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Saktiandi asked whether and what steps have been taken to engage Allianz and if any engagement had been planned.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, we obtained information, we studied them, and once we assessed and decided that it is not in the public interest to proceed with the deal, we thought it is better to take an open and transparent approach in the manner that I have outlined.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Neil Parekh and Mr Mark Lee raised some questions around social mission.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I think Mr Chua, in particular, has related his own experience.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, by definition, there has got to be a level of flexibility, malleability, which allows the parties charged with their social mission to adjust and to take steps to adjust.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In this case, parties would have heard from my Ministerial Statement that Income – and I think earlier on, Members heard Senior Minister of State Desmond Tan speak to that as well – had reiterated that it would discharge its social mission at the point of corporatisation and exemption and also at the point of this transaction.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Specifically, in the case of Income, it has over the years been very clear in seeking to expand its social mission such as providing for the needs of persons with disability, migrant workers, low-income workers.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is how it looks at its social mission portfolio and I am not saying that it may not change down the road.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Depending on the needs of society, that may well need to change.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, in some ways, you have got to give flexibility to the manner in which a social enterprise looks at its mission in the context of the industry that it is in and decides what specific products to raise.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I think Ms He also asked whether one day it could become health insurance.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I, as I said, I am not speaking for Income, but I would not see that it is so unconnected from its current life insurance business that it may well be covered.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But it is something that I express no view on, save to say that I think we need to give some degree of flexibility and malleability to the concept.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I want to also say that the point of applying for exemption from section 88, a point I alluded to earlier, Income did emphasise that it continues to remain strongly committed to its social mission of providing affordable, accessible and sustainable insurance to the underserved communities.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In relation to what Mr Chua said, what Mr Parekh said, that definition by Income itself gives you some indication as to how they see the social mission and how they see themselves discharging that social mission.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Whilst I am on the point about the exemption, Ms He raised a couple of points on the exemption and I would like to address them.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: To recap, I had explained previously the circumstances in which Income, the co-op, proposed to convert its legal status from a co-op into a corporate status.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: There were advantages that it felt it could avail themselves of, such as, for instance, there were limitations on the extent to which dividends could be declared by a co-op and that itself made it less attractive for investors, for strategic partners to come in to work with Income.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It also needed the ability to broaden its capital base.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I think there are some debates about what we mean by capital buffers, capital resiliency.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But what is important to bear in mind in relation to Ms He's question on representations and what was discussed in the context of the corporatisation and the exemption, Income said very clearly it wanted to do better in the insurance business.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It emphasised that it would continue to do its social mission as before, based on a quote I read earlier, and that it would only change its legal form as far as its business was concerned.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: What is also important to bear in mind in the context of the exemption is that section 88 applies, as I explained, in the context of a social co-op seeking to wind up its business, to cease its business, stop altogether and then after paying off its debts and accounting for other charges, it will have surplus or it may have surpluses, which then comes into the consolidated fund.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: That is the raison d'etre behind section 88.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In the context of Income, the co-operative, the raison d'etre, or purpose, is quite different.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: First, it was being liquidated and wound up, it was not ceasing its business.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In fact, on the contrary, it was trying to do its business better in a corporate vehicle that would allow it to reach out to strategic partners, access capital and so on, to do its business better.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It was fundamentally not winding up its business, not stopping.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And therefore, on that basis, it needed to then say, I would also have these surpluses, which I had accumulated before, brought into the new entity.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It was on that basis that we granted the exemption for the surpluses to also flow through into the new corporate entity.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Ms He also asked whether there is a link between surpluses and social mission.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As I had explained earlier, I think we have to give a degree of flexibility to the entity charged with that social mission to decide how to apply it.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In the context of Income, as it stood post-corporatisation, its majority shareholder was NE, also a co-operative.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It also had a number of other smaller minority shareholders, amongst which were also co-operatives.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In that context, we left it to them to decide how you want to carry out your social mission, how you would deploy the surpluses.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: You may offer migrant workers insurance; you might offer mental wellness insurance and so on.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It is something that I think we need to give them a broad remit over, given especially that they have converted into a corporate entity, a point that I made on Monday as well.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: You cannot, on the one hand, say you can corporatise, but on the other hand, you still have to behave as if you are a co-operative entity.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I would add, Sir, that it is not for me to say how Income ought to have structured its transactions with Allianz or with any other party.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As to what is acceptable, it is not for us to speculate, and if the parties, as they have indicated publicly, wish to re-evaluate, reconsider, we will consider that when they have structured any new arrangements.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: She makes the case that the 4 August 2024 statement by Income is misleading.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I think the Member quoted the words "capital resilience" which I think it is paragraph 7 of the statement that she was reading from.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Paragraph 7 talks about the need for the transaction to take place so that Income could build up capital resilience.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Member also spoke about capital buffers coming under pressure and questioned whether that statement is true.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Member also made the point, effectively, that the Member is not able to reconcile the capital reduction with the need for the proposed transaction to seek capital resiliency.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Would I have accurately summarised the Member's contention?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In the context of an insurance company, I think Members would understand that there is a need to maintain a capital adequacy ratio.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The ratio is determined either by reference to the assets you have or the liabilities you carry.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Either one of them can affect your capital adequacy ratio.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And consequently, either one of them can affect your capital resiliency.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: If you increase capital, you can have a better capital adequacy ratio.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Similarly, if you decrease your liabilities, you can also increase your capital resiliency and ratio.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And that is why on Monday I said this statement is not misleading.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: I think we will take clarifications after the political office holders (POHs) have provided their statements.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I note that the WP plans to abstain and is not supporting the Bill.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Members have raised several important considerations relating to the Bill and I will summarise into three categories: first, how to strike a balance between regulations to protect public interest and maintain investor confidence; second, how does the Government ensure that inter-agency information exchange and coordination does not compromise on commercial confidentiality; and finally, clarifications on the capital reduction plan, Bill parameters and coverage.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa, Mr Saktiandi Supaat, Ms Joan Pereira, Mr Neil Parekh, Mr Mark Lee, Ms Usha Chandradas and Mr Yip Hon Weng have recognised the merits of the Government's intervention in this deal, while raising questions about its impact on business confidence and Singapore's role as an international insurance hub.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: They also asked about the likelihood of future Government interventions and how transparency can be maintained to preserve trust in our system.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The same applies to MAS as the financial sector regulator.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We will continue to welcome investors with our business-friendly operating environment.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: When legislative amendments are proposed, the Bills are presented and debated in Parliament in an open and transparent manner.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We would explain the rationale for the proposed changes, just like what we are doing now for this Bill.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: MAS maintains a regulatory approach that is consultative and provides stability and predictability for industry players.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As a standard practice, MAS consults on major policy and legislative changes.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: For complex policies, there could be a series of consultation papers to obtain feedback from stakeholders over an extended period.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This recognises that insurance co-ops are a special category of insurers with a social mission.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The Bill does not affect any other insurer or the financial industry at large.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Saktiandi asked about the Bill's impact on existing free trade agreements for activities in the financial services sector.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It does not impact our free trade agreements.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As I have explained earlier, we do not have concerns with the suitability of Allianz to be a majority shareholder of Income.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Our concerns lie in the terms and structure of this particular deal, and such concerns would apply whether the acquiror is Allianz or any other entity, and whether the acquiror is local or foreign.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: To Mr Neil Parekh's comment that control of Income should not be ceded to foreigners, I would reiterate that the Government agrees with NE's intention and Income's intention to find a strategic partner to strengthen its competitiveness and capital base in the long term so that it can continue to do well to do good.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If the concerns of MCCY can be addressed in a future deal, the Government is open to consider such a proposal, whether it is from a foreign or local entity.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The most important consideration is the outcome – that Income becomes a stronger entity that is able to serve its policy-holders well and fulfil its social mission effectively.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: To Mr Saktiandi's question and also Mr Leong Mun Wai's question on whether we have engaged Allianz, the answer is yes, and they have indicated that they understood the reasons for the Government's decision.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Leong can have a look at their public statement.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Neil Parekh asked how the Government will ensure that any future partner can contribute to the financial strength of Income, while still preserving its social mission.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: MAS has regulatory requirements and guidance in place for insurers to maintain sufficient capital reserves to meet policy-holder claims, including under adverse conditions, and for insurers to have robust risk management frameworks in place.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As an insurer, Income continues to meet these requirements.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: With the Bill, the Minister-in-charge of MAS can, in giving his approval for an entity to obtain effective control or substantial shareholding in Income, impose conditions to ensure Income's commitments to its social mission are upheld post-transaction.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We agree with Mr Mark Lee that businesses should be given an opportunity to address and correct draft plans before final decisions or interventions are made, and this is, in fact, what MAS has done for the proposed transaction.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And as I explained in the House on Monday, information provided to MAS as part of its supervisory dealings with financial institutions, including Income and Allianz, is confidential and not normally shared with other Government agencies.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We recognise that companies submit such information for a specific regulatory purpose and not to enable general Government evaluation.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And as Mr Mark Lee correctly pointed out, some of this information may involve sensitive decisions.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: In this particular instance, Income had special characteristics.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As a former co-op, it had previously been under the regulation of MCCY before its corporatisation.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: MCCY maintains an interest in whether Income continues to perform its social mission, as this was the representation given when Income was allowed to corporatise.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Hence, while conducting its assessment, MAS considered that it was in the public interest to share the information with MCCY.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Ms Joan Pereira and Mr Mark Lee asked whether the information sharing and coordination among agencies could have been done earlier.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: MAS received business projections of the cash remittance in mid-July and was reviewing the information.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: After the Parliamentary Sitting on 6 August, MAS saw that Income's planned capital optimisation and cash remittance could be relevant to MCCY's views on the proposed transaction and shared the information with MCCY.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Ms Jessica Tan, Mr Saktiandi and Mr Raj Joshua Thomas explained this well.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The decision to halt the deal in its current form and the fact that we are here today to debate and approve the amendments to the Insurance Act demonstrate that due process works.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It is about coming to Parliament after putting together the full picture, working across the whole-of-Government to see what is the overall assessment of how to move forward on this important issue, and then coming to Parliament to present the information and proposals for Parliament's approval.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I wish to thank Ms Tan, Mr Saktiandi and Mr Raj Joshua Thomas, and also other Members for their support in clarifying the facts and, importantly, for showing appreciation to our public officers in MAS and MCCY.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As Ms Tan said, they were working hard and they were doing their jobs.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: In contrast, WP's Assoc Prof Jamus Lim and Mr Leong Mun Wai from PSP took a different approach.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The Members made serious allegations regarding our public officers, regarding our agencies.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I do not know why the Members have to take this approach, especially after I had explained what happened on Monday.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Why is it necessary for Mr Leong and Assoc Prof Lim to still want to throw our public officers under the bus?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The officers needed time to go through this plan and because they were not aware of the undertakings and the details of MCCY's exemption that was given earlier.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The exemption was gazetted, but the details and the conditions and the undertakings, those were not made public.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I do not think it is fair for Mr Leong to expect that the MAS team would automatically know what those details are, when those details are not made public.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It was only after we had a fuller understanding of the set of issues after the 6 August Parliament Sitting that the MAS team saw that there could be a connection to what MCCY was looking at.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And then they surfaced this to the Board and then we shared it with MCCY.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I hope that Mr Leong and Assoc Prof Lim could give our officers some credit, could understand what they were going through and also look at it from their perspective, from their point of view.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: They were not trying to do something wrong or, as Assoc Prof Lim mentioned, "to lead to multiple breakdowns of communications", or "to work in a siloed manner".

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That is certainly not what they were trying to do.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: They were trying their very best to do their work.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And when they saw that there was a link, they shared the information.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: They surfaced it to the Board and then we shared the information with MCCY.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And this is how the Government then came together, across different parts of the Government, taking a whole-of-Government approach, coming to Parliament with this Bill, to seek Parliament's approval.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is the outcome of a whole-of-Government effort.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: First, he talked about SIRA, or the Significant Investments Review Act.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And we will look at whether an entity is a key provider of security-related functions, especially when there are a few or no alternatives and whether it is adequately covered by existing sectorial legislation.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, there is a rigorous process to decide what goes into SIRA and I hope Assoc Prof Jamus Lim understands that if we are too quick to put many entities under SIRA, that will go against what many other Members have spoken about earlier, that how then do you maintain investor confidence and have a pro-business operating environment?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, we must have a good basis, a good reason, before we decide that something needs to be designated under SIRA.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Assoc Prof Lim was also incorrect to point out that there are no controls if companies, like DBS and Singtel, were to sell their shares.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I would urge Assoc Prof Lim to check his facts.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: MAS would have to approve any changes in significant shareholding for banks, including DBS, and IMDA would have to approve any changes in significant shareholding for telcos like Singtel.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Saktiandi and Mr Raj Joshua Thomas and, I believe, also Ms He Ting Ru, asked if the Bill only operates prospectively instead of retrospectively and if there would be any issues of retrospective application of the law.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The contractual terms of the transaction clearly state that it is subject to regulatory approval by MAS.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: There is, therefore, no retrospective application of the law.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Saktiandi, Ms He Ting Ru, Ms Hazel Poa and Ms Usha asked if the existing sections 26 and 27 of the Insurance Act would already allow whole-of-Government considerations to be taken into account, since the sections provide that MAS may approve an application, if the Authority is satisfied that the criteria are met.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: To clarify, MAS takes into account all relevant considerations within the objects of the Insurance Act.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: There is currently no explicit provision under the Insurance Act for MAS to take into account the views of MCCY, which include questions relating to social mission, in assessing a proposed acquisition of an insurer with co-operative links.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: MAS did not expand the scope of sections 26 and 27, as MCCY's views would not be relevant for insurers that are not linked to co-operatives.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And this is important, going back to the earlier point that Mr Mark Lee, Mr Neil Parekh and a few others mentioned, which is, we need to make sure that we still keep our operating environment one that is business-friendly and that investors will have confidence to continue to want to invest in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think that is important and that is why we wanted to scope it tightly for this purpose and not have a general clause.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Ms Usha Chandradas also sought clarification on the interpretation of "conduct its business prudently" in the context of Income.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: To Mr Saktiandi's question on whether there should be a comprehensive summary of various classes and target companies, we do not think it is necessary.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The current case involving Income is unique due to its co-operative history and social mission, setting it apart from typical insurers.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: For standard scenarios, the Insurance Act already clearly outlines the specific regulatory approvals required for such transactions.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked whether the proposed capital optimisation measures would weaken the capital adequacy of Income.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As the capital required will increase as business risks increase, insurers may undertake capital optimisation measures, such as reinsurance to reduce the risk retained within the insurer, without shrinking its business or weakening it.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This would, then, reduce the regulatory capital required to support the same business.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: These measures that free up capital to be returned to shareholders is not an uncommon commercial practice, as Mr Liang has pointed out.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And to be clear, in the case of Allianz, they had provided a preliminary business plan to MAS in mid-July regarding the capital reduction.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: There was no application from Allianz for capital reduction.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: First, I think I have clarified that there was no application from Allianz.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: They only provided a preliminary business plan to MAS in mid-July.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I also clarified on Monday and also today and a few Members have mentioned it as well, that the deal is still subject to MAS regulatory approval.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I do have an issue with how Mr Leong has described the capital reduction plan as an asset stripping exercise.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And I do not think that is a fair description.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think Mr Leong deliberately chose that term and this is not the first time I have heard Mr Leong make unkind remarks towards NTUC.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, yes, there is a difference in views between what NTUC, NE, Income have put up and what the Government feels is the right way forward, but we do not disagree with the objectives of why we are doing this or why Income is doing this.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The purpose of doing this is the right one.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It is to strengthen Income and to do well, so that it can do good.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The Members of the Opposition often remind us that just because there are differences in views, it does not mean that we should automatically jump to the conclusion that you have a bad intention.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I respect that view, Sir, so I would like to seek their agreement that, in this case, please also apply that consistently; that just because there is a difference in views, in terms of how the proposal is structured, it does not mean that you should conclude that NTUC and NE were doing this without a good intent.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: However, we remain open to Income entering into a new deal, whether with Allianz or with another entity, if the outcome is that this can help to strengthen Income.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The Minister-in-charge of MAS can then withhold approval if he considers it in the public interest to do so.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The Minister-in-charge of MAS will also take into account prudential considerations under the Insurance Act in making his decision.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I hope I have clarified the concerns raised by Assoc Prof Jamus Lim and Ms He Ting Ru, and I sincerely hope that the WP can support this Bill.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: We have had 19 speakers and the debate has lasted over three hours.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Minister Chee Hong Tat, Minister Edwin Tong and Senior Minister of State Desmond Tan have responded, to all, if not the majority of the questions raised.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Be that as it may, given the urgency of this Bill and it being read the Second and Third time today, I will allow clarifications, but I seek the understanding of Members to keep the clarifications succinct and clear; and that be reciprocated by the front bench in targeted and accurate responses.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: So, I will do my best to allow as much clarification time as I am able to.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: But I feel that it is nevertheless imperative for me to highlight instances where the system that the civil service operates under, which is, to be clear, overseen by this Government, is problematic because our civil servants can only do the best they can within the constraints that they face from the Government of the day.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: So, once again, to reiterate, I am critiquing the system, not the civil servants.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: I do not think it is useful to bring in the civil servants as pawns to a political argument.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: To further clarify, I did not say that there are no protections for the sale of significant assets, like Singtel or DBS, but that additional protections are granted by SIRA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Could I confirm with the Minister that this Government will never consider listing assets, such as DBS or Singtel, under SIRA?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I did not refer to our public officers as pawns and I do not think he should too.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We have deep respect for our public officers.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We know that they work hard, they do their work well and it was not so clear earlier when Assoc Prof Lim was making all the criticisms of working in silos and having breakdowns of communications, that he was referring to the system.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If his concern is about the system, I have also explained on Monday and earlier, what happened and why it was not in the ordinary course of operations for MAS, when they are assessing information from a financial institution, to share that with another Government agency.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If Assoc Prof Lim considers that as a failure, a systems failure, then I presume, maybe he could let me know what his counterproposal is.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Is he then suggesting – and I am not trying to put words in his mouth, I am only asking – that anytime MAS receives information, whether there is a reason or not, we should then share it with all other Government agencies?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I hope that is not what Assoc Prof Lim is proposing.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think that will have an impact on investor confidence and it will affect our pro-business operating environment.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I have explained what happened with this particular case and I have also reiterated the chronology of what happened.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I hope Assoc Prof Lim can accept that account of what happened and not keep repeating unfounded allegations about the public service officers in our system facing constraints from the Government of the day when it comes to sharing of information.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I do not think there is any evidence, unless Assoc Prof Lim can produce evidence; otherwise, I would like him to please withdraw that rather serious allegation.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, in a way that is already covered.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Allow me to do two responses to what the Minister had directed towards me during his speech.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: My first point is also about civil servants, something similar to what Member Assoc Prof Jamus Lim had just said.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Today, I have not said anything about civil servants.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: What I have said is, I would like to acknowledge the effort put in by MCCY and MAS to scrutinise the transaction and come up with this Bill.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, this is an appreciation of the work done by MCCY and MAS.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But I have directed at the Ministers — it is the responsibility of the Cabinet Minister to ensure that they are appraised of all relevant and important information, and to consider them fully before making decisions and public pronouncements.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I am saying that because on 6 August, we spent more than one hour clarifying during Question Time about this whole deal without complete information.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, we are running parallel all the time and you can also say that it was quite a waste of time.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But what happened now is that now, with more information, we know that the Ministers and the NTUC CC, actually, they do not have the information on the capital reduction.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But still, we are concerned about the coordination and how things are being presented before the information is complete.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I want to respond to the Minister when he said that I am bringing in the civil servants and all that, a point that is similar to what Assoc Pro Jamus Lim has said.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The second point that the Minister has said is about my characterising the exercise as asset stripping.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: In finance, nobody with some knowledge about finance would disagree with me.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: It has nothing to do with the intent.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But the plan that you put up, is actually not so good.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: That is why the Government now is coming back after more work and saying, "Oh, this plan cannot go through".

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The plan is not a good plan, from the point of view of continuing with the social mission.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: And I have got one more point to raise afterwards.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: It is that it is also not a plan that provides enough protection to policy-holders.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, it is not fair for the Minister to say that I am trying to characterise the deal in bad light.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Anyone with basic financial knowledge would not disagree with me.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It provided the opportunity for Members to ask questions, and for MCCY and MAS to clarify what is the status of the situation at that time; and then, to hear the concerns of the Members.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think it is not correct and I hope Mr Leong could withdraw that comment too, to describe that process as a waste of time.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The point about whether information should be made known during a discussion, I had clarified repeatedly that when we came to Parliament on 6 August, both Minister of State Alvin Tan and I made it clear that there was no regulatory approval given to the deal.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It is something that is still being evaluated, considered and, therefore, in response to Mr Leong's point about how before we make any decision or pronouncement, we should have the full set of information.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is the decision that we are seeking approval from Parliament.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I do not think there is any departure from what Mr Leong described as what he expects the Government to do.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But on 6 August, there were Parliamentary Questions filed.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Unless Mr Leong is suggesting that we do not answer Parliamentary Questions?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If not, at that point in time, because the deal is still being considered, no approval was given yet, I think it was only correct that we gave replies based on information that we had at that point in time.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But because there was no regulatory approval given, there was no decision or pronouncement by the Government.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The second point that Mr Leong raised, Mr Deputy Speaker – I find it quite odd that Mr Leong on one hand would say he is not trying to characterise it negatively and, on the other hand, he has made it quite clear that this is a bad deal.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We have explained why the capital reduction plan on its own would not be something that is uncommon.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: An entity, whether Income or another insurer, another financial institution, to do capital optimisation, I think Minister Edwin Tong explained this, I explained this as well and Mr Leong, I am sure, understands.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Financial optimisation is something that entities, companies do regularly.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: When MAS was looking at this initially, they were looking at it from a prudential point of view to see – if you do this, would Income still have the necessary capital to meet its capital adequacy ratio?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I would like to suggest that, perhaps, it is not very useful and productive for us to argue about different adjectives being used.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But as Ms Hazel Poa said earlier, we let the public decide which phrase was used by Mr Leong and which phrase was used by me to describe this exercise.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And the Hansard will reflect that Mr Leong did, indeed, say it is an asset stripping exercise.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han
text: For Minister Edwin Tong, it has been a long day so I apologise if I failed to hear this in his response.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han
text: I do understand that the factors were being looked at cumulatively.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han
text: But referencing my speech, can the Minister clarify whether the lack of clear binding provisions or structural protection around Income's social mission alone is sufficient reason to merit the blocking of this deal?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I had mentioned a series of factors that we looked at, one of which is the lack of structural protection.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, this is taken in the context of the suite of terms as well as the circumstances in which the capital reduction was done and the amount, were cumulatively the factors that we took into account, not any one single factor on its own.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: First, I do not seem to recall either of the Ministers clarifying the questions raised by Ms He Ting Ru and Ms Hazel Poa about whether MAS needs this Bill.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: In other words, does MAS not have sufficient power within its current jurisdiction to take into account the public interest in having affordable financial products and, therefore, is this Bill really necessary?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I do not recall either Minister touching on this point.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But Ms Sylvia Lim may have missed it.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, with your permission, Madam, can I just read those sections again?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, this is what I said earlier, that the Bill does not affect any completed transaction because there is no formal application yet by Allianz to obtain effective control and become a substantial shareholder of Income.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And, therefore, there is no retrospective application of the law.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: There is no formal application yet by Allianz.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, yes, we do not disagree that there is a deal that is being considered.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But it is a fact, Sir, that there is no formal application by Allianz to MAS.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: I agree that there are no specific provisions at the moment to take into account MCCY's views, but at the same time, the existing legislation does not prohibit MAS from taking into account those views.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: So, why are sections 26 and 27 not sufficient?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: My second clarification is referring to Minister Edwin Tong's reply that the capital resilience can be improved by re-insuring.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: My point was that the reason for this sale of Income Insurance was presented as the need to improve capital resilience.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: But if the capital resilience is actually improved through re-insurance, then it has nothing to do with this acquisition by Allianz.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: So, why is that presented as the reason?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: First, that itself could lead to more uncertainty for the industry players because they will be wondering, the next time, would you then change the interpretation to something else again without being clear about the reasons why you are doing it and being transparent about how you are doing it.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That is why, as Ms Jessica Tan mentioned earlier, we prefer to take a more open and transparent approach of coming to Parliament to seek Parliament's approval for this change, to address the concerns that we have but to do so in a tightly-scoped manner so that the rest of the industry who are not co-operatives or who have no links to co-operatives need not worry that this new provision taking into account social mission will also apply to them.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Oh, Minister Edwin Tong, do you want to add to Minister Chee's reply?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
